records.title: Client gallery links go dead or vanish, forcing photographers to re-share
records.statement: Delivered client galleries become inaccessible, are removed, archived or expire unexpectedly, so photographers must rebuild galleries and re-send links to past clients.

evidence.summary: Photographers report live client gallery links vanishing after an unannounced storage policy change (Aug 2026) and wedding galleries lost without notice (Jun 2026), forcing restores from backups and re-sharing with many clients.

Another Pic-Time review (Sep 2026) says clients could not open a delivered gallery at all, so the photographer had to recreate and re-upload it. Impact severity 4: loses time and client trust after delivery.
A ShootProof reviewer (Jan 2026) hit confusing archived-gallery behaviour, with charges for archived galleries not visible or controllable in the account.
A Pixieset reviewer (Jul 2021) liked expiry and PIN controls but wanted scheduled expiry notifications so clients are not surprised by a dead link.

records.title: Clients struggle to download images and revisit or make selections in galleries
records.statement: Clients get confused downloading on mobile, cannot find their way back to favorites, or cannot make or submit selections, so photographers end up giving hands-on support after delivery.

evidence.summary: Pixieset reviewers (Feb 2022, Dec 2024) say clients sometimes have a hard time downloading images and mobile saving takes too many steps. A Jul 2021 reviewer says clients struggled to get back to their favorites folder to change picks.
Another Pixieset reviewer (Jul 2021) says clients get a little confused downloading and need step-by-step guidance from the photographer.
A Pic-Time reviewer (Sep 2026) says clients could not make selections or validate them, with blank pages shown, blocking the proofing step.

Long-running Adobe community request thread (started 2015, 61 replies) asks that clients without an account be able to rate, like and comment on shared collections, because forced sign-up blocks client feedback.
A photographer asks how to let 160 headshot clients mark favorites in a password-protected gallery and get the selections back automatically; replies point to several workaround tools, none simple.

records.title: Gallery links get forwarded and photographers cannot control who has access
records.statement: Clients forward or post gallery links, and with link-only access the photographer cannot limit who views or downloads, risking privacy and lost print or download revenue.

evidence.summary: A photographer (Oct 2025) explains that anyone-with-the-link galleries let clients pass links to third parties, and prefers per-invite single-use access tokens so a forwarded invite does not work.
A photographer (Mar 2025) lists unintended access to family, child and boudoir images and lost income when clients obtain files without paying as core risks of gallery sharing.
A wedding photographer (Mar 2025) cites non-clients getting unpaid downloads and parents and boudoir clients worrying images leak, motivating tighter access control.
A feature-request board post (Sep 2024, 46 votes) asks for password-protected galleries with high-res downloads and expiration dates; commenters echo the need.

tier_mapping.notes: WORKS (all tiers, ungated): every /g/{token} render requires an OTP-verified snap-g cookie pinned to that grant (page.tsx resolveGalleryAccess). OTP is emailed ONLY to grant.clientEmail (otp/send: typed email must equal grant.clientEmail, else invalid_email and no mail), Turnstile-gated, 6 digits, 10 min TTL, 5 attempts, caps 30/email/30d, 5/email/15min, 5/IP/hr. So a stranger holding a forwarded link sees the gate with the masked client email and cannot pass without the client inbox. Photographer can set expiry at send (7/30/90/365 or none), edit expiry on an existing link, Revoke (cuts open sessions live), New link (regenerate, old URL dead), Re-send; Galleries page lists states Active/Expiring soon/Expired/Revoked/Regenerated. Route: /dashboard/projects/{id}?tab=gallery -> section Client gallery -> row of link: expiry select (aria Edit expiry), View, Re-send, New link, Revoke (confirm dialog). /dashboard/galleries is READ-ONLY list (no revoke there). Lite+: Activity panel (per-client views, favorites, downloads, last seen; Free sees an upgrade card, canView = plan!=free), download PIN 4-8 digits + web-size (API 403 pin_requires_lite), guests/schedule/notify. Studio: download approvals, watermarks, deterrents, per-photo insights. Per-photo social share cards are Lite+ and children of the gallery (die on revoke). GAPS to keep claims honest: one grant = one client email, no allowed-recipient list or second verified recipient, no single-use/per-device tokens, a verified client browser stays valid 30d, a client can forward the 6-digit code or downloaded files; photographer cannot see failed/stranger attempts (otp_fail/otp_sent are logged in share_access_log but excluded from the Activity panel FAVORITE_EVENTS list); Activity is per client email, no IP/device list. Fallback: env GALLERY_OTP_MODE=off makes the link the only gate (wrangler.jsonc sets otp). PRODUCT BUGS: (1) docs gallery-delivery says expiry 7/30/60/90/365 but the per-link expiry select on the project page offers 7/30/90/1yr/none (60 only in Settings > Delivery); (2) docs gallery-delivery opens with everything ships on every gallery incl. insights text but the Activity panel is Lite+; plans-data.ts has no field for these gates (they live in route handlers), so tier claims must cite routes. EVIDENCE: staging logged in as Studio org (cannot observe Free UI; Free gating is from code: canView and pin_requires_lite). Staging live OTP stranger flow NOT exercised (needs a minted token and inbox); verified by code read plus staging: bogus /g token shows Access denied page, /g/demo-proj-wedding/preview is 404 anonymously and renders for the owner with no OTP and no view counting.

records.title: Free gallery plans limit client downloads to web size, not full resolution
records.statement: On the free tiers of competing gallery tools, clients can only download web-size files, so a photographer who does not pay cannot hand over the real full-resolution photos.

evidence.summary: Vendor pricing page: the Free plan (3 GB) lists no full resolution download; every paid plan from $8/mo (billed annually) lists full resolution download.
Vendor help page: on the Free plan the only download size in galleries is the 2048px social size; clients can download full-resolution images from the entry paid plan up.

2020 photographer forum thread: a free gallery account caps client downloads at 3600px and 3 GB storage, which pushes photographers to compare other hosts. No explicit complaint about download-all itself.

2018 Adobe community thread: a photographer finds clients download re-compressed files (about 5 MB shrinks to about 900 KB) from a web gallery; the answer is to share originals through a plain file-sharing link instead. Related pain on a different product.

Linked by the founder. An automated fetch is blocked (HTTP 403), so this page was NOT read directly; a search snippet of the vendor's help center says original-resolution downloads need an upgraded plan, which the pricing page above corroborates.

history.note: evidence opened 2026-10-04: 2 vendor policy pages read, 2 forum threads read, 1 founder-linked page blocked to automated fetch; see analysis for caveats

analysis.founder_lead: Competitors do not give a full-quality download-all on free tiers (Pixieset help article).
verified_by_reading: Pixieset: Free plan has no full resolution download (pricing page)
CloudSpot: Free plan downloads are 2048px only (help page)
not_verified: Pic-Time: its download permissions article shows high-res and web-size options but no free-vs-paid split
analysis.wording_correction: Competitors DO offer download-all of a gallery. What free plans withhold is full resolution. Do not say 'competitors have no download all'.
analysis.snap_state: WEB-261 (shipped 2026-10-04): download-all on every plan incl. Free, whole gallery/folder/favorites, full resolution by default with EXIF/GPS stripped, streamed ZIP parts up to 2 GiB each. Web-size option and download PIN are Lite+. Proofing galleries deliver watermarked previews only, never originals. See apps/snap/lib/gallery-downloads.ts, lib/zip-delivery.ts, app/api/g/[token]/zip/route.ts.
analysis.who_feels_it: Free-tier and price-sensitive photographers and their clients. This is an acquisition angle (switching from a free competitor plan), NOT a paid-tier trigger, so it will not by itself produce paying users.
analysis.evidence_strength: Moderate-low as a complaint: two vendor policies read directly, two older forum threads about adjacent pain, no first-hand current complaint found (Reddit is blocked in the browser extension).
reel_guardrails: Make claims about Snap only: 'full-resolution download-all on the Free plan'. Do not name Pixieset or any competitor on screen or in the caption.
A comparison like 'many free galleries limit downloads to web size' is only safe as 'some', and only because two were verified.
Say 'full resolution', not 'original untouched files': GPS/EXIF location data is stripped from originals.
Do not claim 'no limit' beyond what the code and docs say; Free has 20 GB storage and 5 active galleries.
Do not show the Lite+ web-size or PIN controls in a zoom; the staging studio is on Studio.
Recording a download touches R2 and creates download events: use the safe staging account only, and never email an unknown address.
